 Stocks To Watch Today (November 16): Kaynes Tech, Meesho, M&M, HDFC, RVNL, Oil India, GAIL and more 
 Written By Varun Yadav • Published: 8:45 AM, Nov 16, 2026 | Updated: 8:45 AM, Nov 16, 2026 Shares of Oil India, Hitachi Energy India, Manappuram Finance, NMDC, Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL), Wakefit Innovations, EIH Ltd and Dilip Buildcon are expected to stay in the spotlight after these companies released their July-September quarter results. Besides earnings, stocks including Zee Entertainment, Meesho, Mahindra & Mahindra, HDFC Bank, GAIL, Kaynes Technology, Bharat Forge and Clean Max Enviro could also witness movement after important corporate announcements.
 Indian stock market is likely to open mildly up, continuing last week's momentum. Gift Nifty traded 0.34 per cent higher at 25,253 around 8:40 AM.
 Shares of Oil India, Kaynes Technology, Hitachi Energy India, Manappuram Finance, NMDC, Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL), Wakefit Innovations, EIH Ltd and Dilip Buildcon are expected to stay in the spotlight after these companies released their July-September quarter results.
 Besides earnings, stocks including Zee Entertainment, Meesho, Mahindra & Mahindra, HDFC Bank, GAIL, Bharat Forge and Clean Max Enviro could also witness movement after important corporate announcements.
 Q2 Results: Oil India, Hitachi Energy, Manappuram Finance, NMDC 
 Oil India: State-owned Maharatna public sector undertaking (PSU) Oil India Limited reported a 21.3 per cent sequential decline in standalone net profit to Rs 2,259.42 crore for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27). The company had reported a net profit of Rs 2,870.21 crore in the April-June quarter.
 Revenue from operations, however, increased 1.4 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to Rs 8,071.33 crore from Rs 7,958.14 crore in the preceding quarter.
 Alongside its quarterly earnings, the company's board declared an interim dividend of Rs 7 per equity share for FY27. Here are the details of the financial performance, dividend announcement and share price movement.
 Numaligarh Refinery processed 803 thousand tonnes of crude oil, and its gross refining margin widened to USD 28.24 per barrel in H1 FY27. Refinery capacity utilisation was 106.26 per cent, up from 103.48 per cent in H1 FY26.
 Hitachi Energy India: The company posted a mixed performance in Q2 FY27. Revenue jumped 64 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,997 crore from Rs 1,833 crore, exceeding the estimated Rs 2,608 crore.
 EBITDA grew 36 per cent to Rs 406 crore from Rs 299 crore but fell short of the estimated Rs 447 crore. EBITDA margin shrank to 13.6 per cent from 16.3 per cent, compared with the estimated 17.1 per cent. Net profit increased 20 per cent to Rs 318 crore from Rs 264 crore.
 Order inflows for the company rose 86 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,121 crore, and its order backlog hit an all-time high of Rs 33,335 crore. Transmission drove order inflows, followed by data centres. During the quarter, export orders rose 41 per cent compared with the same period a year earlier. Margins were nevertheless affected by inflation in commodities.
 Manappuram Finance: The company delivered a strong consolidated performance in Q2 FY27, as net interest income (NII) climbed 45 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,959 crore from Rs 1,354 crore, surpassing the estimated Rs 1,818 crore.
 Net profit jumped 223 per cent to Rs 701 crore from Rs 217.3 crore, against the estimated Rs 660 crore. Provisions came in at Rs 294 crore, compared with Rs 381 crore in the year-ago quarter and Rs 225 crore in the preceding quarter.
 Assets under management (AUM) rose 60 per cent year-on-year, while gold loan AUM increased 92 per cent. Asset quality, however, weakened slightly: gross non-performing assets (GNPA) climbed to 1.8 per cent from 1.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter, and net NPAs rose to 1.2 per cent from 1.1 per cent.
 With branch-opening restrictions now lifted, the company intends to launch 500 new gold loan branches in FY27. Management anticipates profit after tax above Rs 1,500 crore in FY27 and aims for 10 per cent growth in gold AUM next quarter.
 NMDC: The state-owned iron ore producer posted mixed results for Q2 FY27. Revenue rose 6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 6,638 crore from Rs 6,261 crore, exceeding the estimated Rs 6,148 crore.
 EBITDA fell 3.07 per cent to Rs 1,943 crore from Rs 2,004 crore, falling short of the estimated Rs 2,104 crore. EBITDA margin narrowed to 29.3 per cent from 32 per cent, versus the estimated 34.2 per cent. Net profit fell 2 per cent to Rs 1,667 crore from Rs 1,694 crore, below the estimated Rs 1,793 crore.
 Royalty and other levies rose to Rs 2,830 crore from Rs 2,177 crore, while other expenses increased to Rs 973 crore from Rs 571 crore.
 Iron ore production climbed 19 per cent year-on-year to 121.55 lakh tonnes, the highest second-quarter output on record. Sales, however, fell 2 per cent to 104.83 lakh tonnes. In H1 FY27, production rose 23 per cent to a record 272.72 lakh tonnes, while sales were broadly flat at 222.13 lakh tonnes.
 Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL): The railway infrastructure company's consolidated Q2 FY27 results were mixed, though margins improved. Revenue fell 8.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,701 crore from Rs 5,123 crore. EBITDA rose 19 per cent to Rs 263 crore, up from Rs 221 crore.
 EBITDA margin rose to 5.6 per cent from 4.3 per cent, and net profit increased 8.7 per cent to Rs 250 crore from Rs 230 crore. Other expenses came down to Rs 51 crore from Rs 72 crore.
 Reliance Power: The company posted weak consolidated results for Q2 FY27. Revenue fell 7.3 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,830 crore from Rs 1,974 crore. EBITDA dropped 17.1 per cent to Rs 512 crore from Rs 618 crore, and EBITDA margin narrowed to 28 per cent from 31.3 per cent.
 Net profit fell 65.5 per cent to Rs 30 crore from Rs 87 crore.
 Wakefit Innovations: The company delivered a mixed consolidated performance in Q2 FY27. Revenue grew 19.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 452 crore from Rs 377 crore, and EBITDA climbed 22.7 per cent to Rs 50 crore from Rs 41 crore.
 EBITDA margin rose to 11.1 per cent from 10.8 per cent. Net profit, however, was nearly unchanged at Rs 15.89 crore, compared with Rs 15.96 crore in the same quarter last year.
 EIH Ltd: The company delivered a solid consolidated performance in Q2 FY27. Revenue grew 16.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 694 crore from Rs 598 crore. EBITDA climbed 22.8 per cent to Rs 189 crore from Rs 154 crore, and EBITDA margin rose to 27.2 per cent from 25.7 per cent.
 Net profit rose 19.9 per cent to Rs 136 crore from Rs 114 crore.
 In a separate development, the company approved construction of a Trident hotel on its 8.89-acre land parcel near Shamshabad Airport in Hyderabad. The project will require an investment of Rs 777 crore and is expected to begin operations by September 2030.
 Dilip Buildcon: The infrastructure company's consolidated performance in Q2 FY27 was mixed. Revenue grew 16.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,250 crore from Rs 1,926 crore. EBITDA, however, fell 6.8 per cent to Rs 439 crore from Rs 471 crore.
 The EBITDA margin narrowed to 19.5 per cent from 24.4 per cent, while net profit dropped 45.5 per cent to Rs 99 crore from Rs 181 crore.
 Corporate action and business updates: Stocks to Watch 
 Meesho: Shares of the e-commerce company could stay in the spotlight, with a block deal valued at about Rs 1,174 crore expected. SVF II is likely to offload a 1 per cent stake in the company at a floor price of Rs 246 per share, a 3 per cent discount.
 Page Industries: The company stated that it does not anticipate any operational impact from the FEMA-related issue. As per management, the amount involved in the case is Rs 48 crore, and the penalty may be around 0.75 per cent of that amount. In a worst-case scenario, the penalty could reach up to three times the amount involved.
 Zee Entertainment: The company's board cleared a share buyback via the tender route at Rs 91 per share, a 23.8 per cent premium to the current market price. The company will repurchase 6.59 crore shares at an estimated cost of about Rs 600 crore. The record date for the buyback has been set at November 25.
 Mahindra & Mahindra: The automaker posted higher production and sales in October. Total production climbed to 1.23 lakh units from 94,873 units a year earlier. Total sales increased to 1.26 lakh units from 1.18 lakh units. Exports grew to 7,241 units from 4,079 units.
 Navin Fluorine International: The company has begun commercial production of R32 at its Surat plant under the additional HFC capacity. The new capacity will be up to 15,000 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA) in R32 equivalent terms. The company had approved an investment of Rs 236.50 crore to set up the capacity, which will be ramped up gradually.
 HDFC Bank: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved the reappointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as Executive Director (ED) of the bank. The reappointment takes effect from November 23 for a one-year term.
 NBCC (India): The company signed several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with the West Bengal government for various development projects. These comprise the redevelopment of the College Street area and Tangra's China Town, as well as the development of river ghats in Howrah and Nabadwip.
 GAIL: The company signed a memorandum of understanding with Krishak Bharati Cooperative Limited (KRIBHCO) to work jointly on a gas-based fertiliser project in Andhra Pradesh. The proposed project will involve establishing a urea manufacturing plant with a production capacity of 1.27 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA) through a joint venture.
 TVS Motor Company: The company reinforced its presence in Mauritius through a new distribution partnership with Le Warehouse. As part of the arrangement, Le Warehouse will serve as the company's reseller. TVS Motor also introduced the TVS Ronin and TVS NTORQ XP in the market.
 Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals: The company intends to set up a captive power project in Gujarat with 19.8 MW of wind capacity and approximately 25 MWp of solar capacity. It will acquire a 26 per cent stake in FPEL Bhanu Private Limited, a special purpose vehicle of Fourth Partner Energy, while Fourth Partner Energy's SPV will hold the remaining 74 per cent stake.
 Union Bank of India: The bank invested about Rs 337 crore in its joint venture company, Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance (SUD Life). As a result of the investment, its stake in the insurance company rose to 26.24 per cent.
 Welspun Corp: The company formed a joint venture with Perma-Pipe Qatar to set up an internal fusion-bonded epoxy (IFBE) coating facility in India. Welspun Corp acquired a 49 per cent stake in WSCPL, while Perma-Pipe Qatar took the remaining 51 per cent. The joint venture will carry out internal FBE coating of steel pipes and related activities.
 Kaynes Technology: The company signed a term sheet with Vishay to set up a semiconductor joint venture in India. The proposed venture will concentrate on semiconductor back-end manufacturing, including wafer processing, assembly, testing and packaging (OSAT).
 Clean Max Enviro: The company signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh government to invest approximately Rs 50,000 crore in a clean energy complex. The project will comprise 3 GW of wind and solar energy capacity and 1 GW of pumped storage capacity. It also intends to establish a 2 GW green compute factory in Kurnool.
 The company aims to develop at least 1.5 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2029, and the entire project is expected to be developed over the next five years.
 Bharat Forge: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved the resolution plan for Tork Motors Private Limited.
 WeWork India: The company leased 3.14 lakh square feet of office space in Hyderabad, adding a capacity of around 4,256 desks. The capacity addition will involve an investment of around Rs 144 crore, which will be financed through internal accruals and debt.
 Dynacons Systems & Solutions: The company secured its first international order from the Commonwealth of Dominica, worth USD 6.83 million. The order involves setting up IT infrastructure across three hospitals, 49 health centres and two wellness centres.
 The scope includes supply, installation, configuration and maintenance, with the project scheduled to be completed over three years. The order marks the company's entry into the Caribbean market.
